newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed lower on Tuesday, spending most of the session just below Monday's record high closing before plunging in the last hour or so of business in response to stronger than expected U.S. economic data.

The AEX share index closed 6.06 points lower at 806.13, making the bulk of its decline after news the U.S. May consumer confidence index surged to 127.1 from 118.5 in April -- a 28 year high and above expectations centred around 114.4.
The AEX index at the outset spiked up to a new trading high of 813.32, beating the 812.87 all-time high set on Monday, but then drifted on light profit-taking in response to recent gains.
"We were taking our tone from Wall Street and went down even though our bond market was a bit better after being lower," said one senior salesman.
Dealers said trading was down to low levels with investors intially happy to trim positions after gains which have brought the AEX up from 787 in the last week.
"This market really is digesting the gains we've had in the last week or so. You can't expect the AEX to go up a few points every day so this is a natural pause," said a dealer.
The AEX index has broken a series of records since May 20 when the U.S. decided to leave interest rates unchanged.
Dealers said some of the market's attention had been diverted by the Dutch government's tap sale of a 5.75 percent ten-year benchmark bond, which was reopened on Tuesday.

The finance ministry said late on Tuesday tap sales during the day had raised 1.9 billion guilders. Tap sales of the bond, first issued in January, reopened on Tuesday and will continue daily between 0700 GMT and 1500 GMT until further notice.

Trading was largely featureless although semi-conductor equipment maker ASML had an erratic session, first climbing on rumours a major competitor was thinking about stepping out of the sector, then dipping when this was denied.

ASML closed 0.60 guilders down 103.00 after touching a high of 106.50 guilders on talk that Japan's Canon was considering moving out of the wafer stepper market, leaving the Dutch firm to move up to second in the market from third.
A quick denial from Canon pricked the share price and it settled back. The shares have bounded up from 80 guilders at the beginning of the month boosted by broker's recommendations.

Philips fell 0.80 guilders to 108.30, moving in line with the market, and showing little reaction to news it agreed to sell its 25 percent minority in Bang & Olufsen to the Danish firm's holding company for around 160 million guilders.
